subject: environmental-science
title: Habitats & Adaptations: Water & Underground
welcome_lead: From deep oceans to dark soil — life adapts to almost everywhere.
meta_desc: KS3 environmental science: aquatic and underground adaptations.
final_note: Even the strangest habitats have specialist residents.

concepts.def: Body parts that take oxygen from water.
Shaped to slip through water easily.
Underground mammal with strong digging paws.
Burrowing soil animal that eats dead leaves.

walkthroughs.body_html: Fish breathe through gills. Their bodies are streamlined to cut through water. Some deep-sea fish make their own light — bioluminescence.
The mole has shovel-like paws and tiny eyes — sight is no use in tunnels. Earthworms have no eyes either but feel vibrations.
In dark places, hearing, smell and touch matter more. Some species lose colour or eyes over generations.

mcqs.q: Why is a cold winter not evidence against climate change?
options: Cold winters are caused by warming.
Bacteria produce them.
Climate refers to long-term averages, not individual weather events.
It is evidence - if it gets cold sometimes, warming must be wrong.

mcqs.q: Why are invasive species often more harmful than native species?
options: They are larger than native species.
Bacteria produce them.
They are inherently more aggressive than native species.
They lack natural predators or competitors in their new environment, so they spread unchecked.

mcqs.q: How are most microplastics formed in the environment?
options: Larger plastic items break down physically into smaller fragments over time.
They are all manufactured at microscopic size deliberately.
They are larger than native species.
Bacteria produce them.
